description:
Get the results of a completed job.

SpiderSite results (type spiderSite, which is what scrape_website submits) carry data.shop: which shop system the website runs and how big its catalogue is. Fields: is_shop, platform, platform_version, confidence, signals, unknown_reason, size {product_count, product_count_source, product_count_is_estimate, sitemap_truncated, languages, currency, ...}, size_tier (XS..XL, computed by the server from size.product_count), detector_version, checked_at.
  * data.shop = null means NOT MEASURED — the detector never ran on that job (every job finished before it shipped is null). It never means "not a shop".
  * Read is_shop; never infer it from platform. platform "wix" with is_shop false is a common, correct answer. is_shop null = the site was checked and the detector could not tell; unknown_reason says why.
  * product_count_is_estimate true = counted from the sitemap, not the shop system's own number. sitemap_truncated true = product_count is a LOWER bound.
  * format "md" renders the block as a Shop section; json and yaml return it as-is.

A RESEARCH job (research_website, or a spiderSite job with mode "research") carries data.research: answer (shaped by the answer_schema you sent; null = the sources do not say it), answer_schema_valid, answer_urls {checked, ungrounded — URLs in the answer that no page read contains}, sources[] {url, title, author, published_at, passages, cited}, pages_read, pages_skipped_robots, usage {model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens}. data.research is null on every other job. format "md" puts the answer and its sources first.

SpiderSite results also carry data.ads: whether the website carries advertising tags. Fields: verdict, unknown_reason, platforms, platform_count, found_in, ids, tag_manager {ids, read, outcome, paused}, consent_manager, martech, spend_tier (low 1 platform · medium 2 · high 3+, computed by the server), detector_version, checked_at.
  * verdict has THREE answers — advertises · no_ad_tag_found · could_not_tell (unknown_reason says why). data.ads = null means NOT MEASURED, never "no ads".
  * Never tell anyone a business does not advertise: no_ad_tag_found only means no ad tag was on the pages read, and a third of the shops with no tag at all were still running Google ads.
  * advertises means an ad tag is configured on the site — evidence of an ad account, not proof of live spend. found_in says where each platform was seen: page · consent_parked · shopify_app are the site's own markup; tag_manager alone means it sat inside a tag-manager container, and one container can serve many unrelated sites of one agency — that is why the stored answer for such a site has confidence "medium", not "high".
  * spend_tier counts platforms: breadth, not money, and never a size signal (size is data.shop.size_tier).
  * data.ads is this job's attempt. The answer KEPT per domain — verdict, platforms, spend tier, confidence — is filterable as crawl.ads_* (list_bulk_corpus_fields); a later could_not_tell never replaces a kept answer.
  * format "md" renders it as an Ads section.

A BULK LEAD SOURCING parent job (the job_id submit_bulk_lead_sourcing returns) answers with a FUNNEL summary — counts per stage — not the leads. Read the leads through IDAP with campaign_id = "bulk_" + the bulk_job_id with its dashes removed; the dashed form matches nothing and returns an empty list, not an error.

job_id.description: Job ID to get results for

workspace.description: Tenant to target (cli_…). Omit to use the active/bound workspace. list_workspaces shows the options.

name: get_job_results
